title: Grateful Dead Live at O'Keefe Center on 1967-08-04

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with good clarity captures a stellar Viola Lee Blues performance, the show's highlight.
ai_review.review: The fragment from this 1967 show shines thanks to an explosive 20‑minute rendition of “Viola Lee Blues,” where Jerry’s lead work is repeatedly praised as “smokin’” and uniquely inventive.  Sound quality is generally clear with only a faint hiss and a tape cut‑off at the end, making it a solid soundboard source for early Dead fans.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (mostly 4‑5) and repeated praise of the Viola Lee Blues indicate a strong performance; recording is described as clear with minor hiss, yielding an overall excellent listening experience.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp soundboard capture; slight tape hiss noted and the tape cuts off before the end of the set, but overall clarity is high.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Only two songs from the show are present; the fragment centers on a powerful Viola Lee Blues that dominates the listening experience despite the incomplete set.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is repeatedly described as ‘smokin’, inventive, and one of his best early‑year performances.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass counterpoint is noted for adding depth to the improvisation, especially in the early‑70 style comment about his role up to 1975.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob’s vocals are mentioned as better than usual on Born Cross‑Eyed; occasional criticism of vocal quality on New Potato.
